semantic_contract: Insert one 4-byte element into a {first, last, capacityEnd} slot array at an arbitrary position, growing the array when it is full, and maintain an intrusive attach/detach protocol on the payload objects the slots point at. The invariants: (1) The arm is chosen solely by `last == capacityEnd`. (2) The container keeps ONE spare slot at [last] that mirrors the last used element; before any move on the in-capacity arm the last element is copied into that spare slot and slot +0x4 is run on it, so the spare slot owns a reference of its own. (3) The element move is skipped entirely when the incoming and displaced pointers are equal, so no virtual call happens for a self-move; only `last` advances. (4) The move runs slot +0x4 on the value entering a slot and slot +0x8 on the value leaving one, matching 0x005c1dc0 slot for slot. (5) On the in-capacity arm the caller's value slot is an IN/OUT parameter: it is overwritten with the value that was moved, and the value it held is detached. (6) The grow arm doubles the capacity (forcing 1 for an empty container and producing a NULL block, with no allocation at all, when the doubling overflows to 0), allocates capacity*16 bytes through the EASTL allocator with the literal tag 'Editor' at allocator.h:209, copies [first, position) and then shifts [position, last) up one slot, installs the caller's value in the hole with slot +0x4, and releases the old block only when both the block and the allocator cookie in front of it are non-null. (7) The receiver triple is rewritten last, in the order last, first, capacity, with the capacity end computed as new_block + capacity*4 bytes. STRUCTURAL CAVEAT, recorded rather than smoothed over: on the in-capacity arm the shift port receives the function's SECOND argument as its loop's exclusive lower bound, while the slot that receives the moved value is derived from the FIRST argument. Those two agree only when the second argument is itself a slot inside the array. Both inspected callers pass a stack address and only ever enter the grow arm, so the in-capacity arm is reproduced structurally and is NOT claimed to be a correct general-purpose insert.
classification_rationale: The grow arm -- the only arm any inspected caller reaches -- is read end to end: 133 instructions, exact capacity arithmetic including the two special cases, two memcpys with their exact length expressions, the allocator call with all six arguments and the live 'Editor' tag string, the cookie-guarded release, and the receiver triple rewritten in the observed order. The attach/detach slot roles are corroborated across five bodies in this batch and in 0x005c1dc0's own disassembly. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC for three named reasons: (1) the two virtual slots have no concrete callee and no located vtable, since the payload type is only known at runtime; (2) the in-capacity arm's element algebra is not established, for the reason given in the contract above -- the shift loop's bound and the hole position are derived from different arguments and cannot both be right for a general position; (3) the container's own type is bounded rather than established: the cEditor + 0x160 correspondence is an SDK offset match on a field the SDK itself comments as 'we only know it calls the DefaultRefCounted* destructor', and the Palettes caller's container at + 0x70 matches no SDK class at all.
semantic_findings: 0x005c8480 is the out-of-line slow half of a push_back, not a general insert, in every observed use. Two independent callers inline the fast half (advance `last`, store, run slot +0x4) and branch to this function only when `last >= capacityEnd`.

The container keeps a spare slot one past the used range holding a duplicate of the last element, and that duplicate gets its own slot +0x4 call. This is why `last` is a valid dereference target in a function that appears not to use it, and it is the most easily misread part of the body.

The capacity is doubled, but the ALLOCATION SIZE is four times the capacity in slots (three ADD EAX,EAX in total). A 4-byte element array therefore over-allocates by 4x, which is either a deliberate slot granularity or padding; static evidence does not say which.

A capacity of 0 after doubling is special-cased to a NULL block with no allocation, after which the function still performs both memcpys -- on a null destination. That is a latent defect in the shipped build, observed statically, not hypothesised.
An empty container forces capacity 1 rather than 2, so the first allocation is exactly one slot.

The old block is released only when the dword immediately before it is non-zero, which is the EASTL allocator's own allocation cookie. Copying the container by memcpy would therefore leak, and the reconstruction preserves the check.

The allocation site is recorded in the binary as tag 'Editor' at EASTL/allocator.h line 209, on a build agent path under c:\BuildAgent\max-spore001-spore\. The same tag appears at a different line (0xac) in cEditor::CommitEditHistory, so the tag is per-subsystem, not per-function.

Argument 2 is an in/out parameter. On the in-capacity arm it is overwritten with the moved value; on the grow arm the Palettes caller at 0x005c8a8f reads it back and runs slot +0x8 on it, which is direct evidence that the value survives the call.

Slots +0x4 and +0x8 are consistently attach-shaped and detach-shaped respectively across 0x005c1dc0, 0x005c8480, 0x0045ac20 and 0x00573c00. This is a cross-body observation about slot behaviour; neither slot is named.
unresolved_questions: What is the element type, and hence what class owns the vtable whose slots +0x4 and +0x8 are called? The payload is reached only through the container's slots at runtime, so no vtable can be located statically.

Is the in-capacity arm reachable with a position strictly inside the array by any caller? Both inspected callers pass `last` and take the grow arm. If some of the other 19 callers pass an interior position, the argument-bound mismatch between 0x005c1dc0's loop and the hole position becomes live, and the arm's element algebra must be re-derived.
Why is the allocation size capacity*16 bytes for 4-byte elements? Either the slot granularity is deliberately 4x, or this is a bug. Nothing in the binary or the SDK distinguishes the two.
